about.title: About FHA Loan Calculator - Government-Backed Home Financing Tool
about.description: The FHA Loan Calculator is a specialized home financing tool designed to help homebuyers calculate monthly payments and benefits for FHA-insured mortgages. FHA loans are government-backed mortgages that offer lower down payment requirements (as low as 3.5%), more flexible credit requirements, and competitive interest rates. This calculator helps you understand FHA loan benefits, calculate monthly payments including mortgage insurance premiums, and compare FHA loans with conventional financing options.

howTo.title: How to Use the FHA Loan Calculator

steps.title: Home Price
steps.description: Enter the purchase price of the home you're considering buying.

steps.title: Down Payment
steps.description: Input your down payment amount (minimum 3.5% for FHA loans with credit scores 580+).

steps.title: Interest Rate
steps.description: Enter the FHA loan interest rate offered by your FHA-approved lender.

steps.title: Loan Term
steps.description: Select the loan term (typically 15 or 30 years for FHA loans).

steps.title: Credit Score
steps.description: Input your credit score to determine down payment requirements and rates.

steps.title: MIP Calculation
steps.description: Review mortgage insurance premium costs (both upfront and annual MIP).

tips: FHA loans require mortgage insurance for the life of the loan if down payment is less than 10%
Credit scores as low as 500 may qualify with 10% down payment
FHA loan limits vary by county - check local limits
Consider gift funds from family members for down payment assistance

faq.a: FHA loans require a minimum credit score of 580 for 3.5% down payment, or 500-579 for 10% down. You need steady employment history, debt-to-income ratio under 43%, and the property must be your primary residence and meet FHA standards.

faq.q: How much is FHA mortgage insurance?
faq.a: FHA loans require upfront MIP of 1.75% of the loan amount, plus annual MIP ranging from 0.45% to 1.05% depending on loan term, loan-to-value ratio, and loan amount. Annual MIP is paid monthly as part of your mortgage payment.

faq.q: Can FHA mortgage insurance be removed?
faq.a: For loans with down payments of 10% or more, MIP is removed after 11 years. For down payments less than 10%, MIP remains for the life of the loan and can only be removed by refinancing to a conventional loan.

FHA loan limits vary by county and are set annually. For 2024, the baseline limit is $498,257 for most areas, with higher limits up to $1,149,825 in expensive markets. Limits are higher for multi-unit properties.
